title: Cartesian pushout products of Kan cells
statement: Use the simplicial sets, monomorphisms, boundaries, horns and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ be a boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ ($m\geq0$) or a horn inclusion $\Lambda^m_k\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ ($m\geq1$), and let $j:P\hookrightarrow Q$ be a monomorphism of small simplicial sets. The Cartesian pushout product $i\mathbin\square j:(Q\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times L)\to Q\times L$ is a monomorphism. It is a weak homotopy equivalence if $i$ is a horn inclusion or if $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: The simplicial-set Kan--Quillen pushout-product argument (cartesian monoidal model structure), with the horn and boundary generators; source copy WANTED.

proof.text: In each simplicial degree, the pushout \((Q\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times L)\) is the set-theoretic union of the images of \(Q\times K\) and \(P\times L\) inside \(Q\times L\). Since \(i\) and \(j\) are degreewise injections, two representatives with the same image in \(Q\times L\) agree coordinatewise; if they come from the two summands, their common point lies in \(P\times K\) and is identified by the pushout relation. Thus the induced map \(i\mathbin\square j\) is injective in every degree, hence a monomorphism.

source.place: Cartesian pushout-product construction for simplicial sets; source copy WANTED.

proof.text: Suppose $i$ is a horn inclusion $\Lambda^m_k\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$. A Kan fibration is by definition a map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion, so $i$ has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration, i.e. $i$ is anodyne in the sense of [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Apply that node with the monomorphism $j:P\hookrightarrow Q$ as its first factor ($A=P$, $B=Q$) and the anodyne map $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ as its second factor ($C=K$, $F=L$): the map $(Q\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times L)\to Q\times L$ it produces is exactly $i\mathbin\square j$, which is therefore anodyne. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] the Kan fibrations are the fibrations of a model structure whose cofibrations are the monomorphisms and whose weak equivalences are the weak homotopy equivalences. An anodyne map $f:X\to Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: factor $f=p\circ g$ with $g$ a monomorphism and weak homotopy equivalence and $p$ a Kan fibration; lifting in the square with $g$ on top, $f$ on the left, $p$ on the right and $1_Y$ at the bottom gives $r$ with $pr=1_Y$ and $rf=g$, so $f$ is a retract of $g$ in the arrow category, and weak equivalences are closed under retracts. Hence $i\mathbin\square j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Cartesian monoidal model structure: horn generators are trivial cofibrations and the pushout-product axiom; source copy WANTED.

proof.text: Suppose instead that $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Since $j$ is also a monomorphism, it is a trivial cofibration of the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], so by the lifting axiom of that model structure it has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration: $j$ is anodyne in the sense of [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Apply that node with the monomorphism $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ as its first factor ($A=K$, $B=L$) and the anodyne map $j$ as its second factor ($C=P$, $F=Q$): the map $(L\times P)\amalg_{K\times P}(K\times Q)\to L\times Q$ is anodyne. The coordinate flips $L\times P\cong P\times L$, $K\times P\cong P\times K$, $K\times Q\cong Q\times K$, $L\times Q\cong Q\times L$ are natural, so they induce an isomorphism of the two pushouts compatible with the maps to $L\times Q\cong Q\times L$; this identifies the map with $i\mathbin\square j$ in the arrow category, and the left lifting property is invariant under such isomorphisms, so $i\mathbin\square j$ is anodyne. As in Step 2 (factorization and retract argument in the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]), an anodyne map is a weak homotopy equivalence, so $i\mathbin\square j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. For $m=0$, $i=\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$ and $i\mathbin\square j\cong j$, consistent with this case.

split_report.summary: Audited the Kan--Quillen cartesian pushout-product statement. The monomorphism clause is proved degreewise by the set pushout union calculation. Both weak-equivalence clauses use the existing Mathlib anodyne pushout-product leaf: a horn inclusion is anodyne by the definition of Kan fibrations, and a monomorphic weak homotopy equivalence is a trivial cofibration hence anodyne by the lifting axiom of the Kan--Quillen model structure; the second case needs the coordinate flip. Anodyne maps are weak homotopy equivalences by the factorization/retract argument. (Maintainer reader fix: the delivered statement-only helper for an arbitrary monomorphism and weak equivalence, strictly stronger than needed, was dropped and Step 3 rewritten through the anodyne leaf.)
